Getting Started

Q: I just installed IFU Analyzer. Where do I start?

A: Follow these steps:

  1. Read Quick Start for a five-minute overview

  2. Get some sample data (or find your own FITS cube)

  3. Launch the application: python main.py

  4. File → Open FITS to load your first data cube

  5. Explore the interface following the Quick Start guide

Q: What FITS data can I use?

A: Any standard FITS cube with:

  • 2D or 3D data (images or cubes)

  • Wavelength calibration in the FITS header

  • A valid coordinate system (optional but useful for sky-aware tools)

Confirmed supported instruments: MUSE, ALMA, MIRI, NIRSpec. Generic 2D FITS images are also supported in the 2D Dual Image Viewer.

Data & Files

Q: Where do I find example data?

A: IFU Analyzer doesn’t include sample data. You’ll need to:

  • Use your own observational data

  • Download public archive data

  • Ensure it’s in standard FITS format

Q: How large can cubes be?

A: Practically limited by your computer’s RAM. Memory-mapped access is enabled automatically for large files, so very large cubes can still be opened — analysis steps will of course run slower on huge cubes.

Q: I get an error opening a file. What’s wrong?

A: Try:

  1. Verify the file is a valid FITS

  2. Check that the FITS header parses correctly

  3. Confirm required keywords are present (INSTRUME, TELESCOP help the instrument auto-detection; CTYPE1/CTYPE2 and a valid CD matrix or CDELT are needed for sky-aware tools)

Q: Why is cube fitting so slow?

A: Large cubes are slow because:

  • There are many pixels to process

  • Each pixel requires non-linear curve fitting

  • Solutions: use fewer cores, restrict to a smaller wavelength range, or fit a subset region first

Troubleshooting

The following items cover the issues reported most often. Each maps to a concrete fix.

Memory errors

  • Close other memory-hungry applications.

  • Try a smaller cube or a subset wavelength range.

  • IFU Analyzer automatically uses memory mapping for large files; you don’t need to enable it manually.

Display issues

  • Make sure PyQt5 is properly installed (pip install PyQt5).

  • Update graphics drivers if rendering is glitchy or windows flicker.

  • Try a different color scale (Log, Power) for better contrast in faint-emission cubes.

File loading errors

  • Verify the file format matches a supported instrument or is a generic 2D/3D FITS.

  • Check the FITS header for the keywords used by instrument detection (INSTRUME, TELESCOP).

  • Ensure the file is not truncated or corrupted.

  • 2D FITS images are supported natively in the 2D Viewer.

WCS grid not visible

  • Confirm the FITS header contains CTYPE1/CTYPE2 with an RA/Dec projection (e.g. RA---TAN, DEC--TAN).

  • Check the terminal output for DEBUG rebuild_axes messages confirming the WCS parse status.

  • Non-celestial WCS automatically falls back to plain pixel axes.

Superimpose misalignment

  • Look in the terminal for DEBUG superimpose: Peak separation — it should be < 0.5 px.

  • A large separation indicates a WCS header discrepancy between the two files (e.g. different EQUINOX, mis-set CRPIX, or a missing CD matrix).

Slides Convolute / Batch Convolution issues

  • If the output sum differs noticeably from the input, both files must have a valid CDELT or CD matrix in their headers — the pixel scale is required to compute the Gaussian kernel size.

  • The flux audit (Ratio out/in) should always read 1.000000. Any large deviation indicates a corrupted WCS header.

  • “Same resolution” is the expected message when both panels have identical pixel scales — no action needed.

  • A “No Sky Overlap” warning means the loaded images cover disjoint sky regions; load images of the same field.

Gaussian fitting issues

  • Ensure an adequate wavelength range is selected (>4 points).

  • Check for positive peaks after baseline subtraction.

  • x0 is infeasible errors are handled automatically with bounds clamping; they’re informational.

  • A low success rate usually indicates noise-dominated regions — try restricting the spatial area or improving the continuum subtraction first.

Performance issues

  • Gaussian mapping is optimized to ~10–30 seconds for typical cubes.

  • Large cubes (>100k pixels) may take 1–2 minutes.

  • Background processing prevents the GUI from freezing during fits.

  • Batch Convolution on many large images may take a few minutes per file (reprojection is pixel-exact, pure Python).

CLI (clip.py) issues

  • Run clip.py from the project root, not from inside cube_explorer/.

  • If you see ImportError: Could not import CubeData, move clip.py one directory level up.

  • The --params flag for auto-continuum expects all seven values in order: window sigma width distance exclusion iters smoothing.
